planting.note: Plant a rooted cutting in spring against a sturdy trellis or arbor in loamy, moist, well-drained soil; shelter young spring growth from late frosts.

directions: Actinidia melanandra is a vigorous Chinese climbing species native to mountain forests of Hubei, Sichuan, and Yunnan, distinct from the familiar arguta and deliciosa kiwis for its rounded, hairless fruit that ripens to a deep reddish-purple skin and flesh. It is one of the parent species behind red-fleshed hardy kiwi hybrids, but the straight species itself remains a little-grown curiosity rather than a commercial fruiting plant. As a dioecious vine it needs both a male and female plant nearby to set any crop, and new spring growth is notably frost-tender even though the established vine itself is reliably cold hardy. Give it a sheltered site with moist, humus-rich loam and a permanent trellis or arbor, since it climbs vigorously once established.
